---
title: "Comparison at matched disclosure"
subtitle: "3.7 · eight simulated units; frontier after the postrank theory book, ch. 22"
description: "How many more errors a rule expects than the best report at the same disclosure."
---

Stating more pairs creates more chances to err. Compare each rule's expected wrong directions with H(N), the lowest count achievable in the report family—including two-report mixtures—at that same disclosure N.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Same N, τ .20.** Posterior-mean tiers state 21 pairs with E 3.11 against H(21) = 2.95, a gap of .163. Open **Method and matched-disclosure benchmark** for mixture chance .667 and the best single report at that N (E 3.013).
- **Estimate tiers.** Three estimate tiers also state 21 pairs, leaving a larger gap of .643.
- **Flags.** Standardized evidence flags state 19 pairs on the frontier: gap 0.
- **Strict order, τ .05.** Stating all 28 pairs leaves gap .230, with risk above all-withheld as τ drops while the matched-N gap stays fixed.
- **At most three grades.** Among 6,051 capped reports, three estimate tiers have gap .480 while posterior-mean tiers reach the capped endpoint.
- **Four tiers outside the cap.** Four tiers lie outside this family (no H benchmark); all-withheld sits at N 0.

<details>
<summary>Scope and lottery notes</summary>

We evaluate all rules under the same posterior. The flags use the mean of all thirty league estimates as their
reference, even when the comparison covers eight units. Each draw from a frontier lottery produces one complete
report with its own disclosure count. The lottery's error fraction divides its expected wrong count by its
expected disclosure. This benchmark concerns pairwise directions under the chosen posterior and loss.

</details>

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}

The package's synthetic `pr_example_gaussian` poverty example uses its own thirty sites. At τ .25 with at most four
grades, this prints quantile cuts with N 337 and risk .1758, versus optimal cuts with N 303 and risk .1603. The risks correspond to different N; H(m) is not a package output.

```r
library(postrank)
w <- c(poverty=1, frl=0, snap=0); s <- postrank_settings(weights=w, tau=.25, G_max=4L); sc <- pr_example_gaussian$means[, "poverty"]
sapply(c("quantile", "optimal"), function(r) unlist(postrank_cuts(sc, pr_example_gaussian, s, direction="descending", rule=r)$evaluation[c("N", "primary_risk")]))
```

:::
